sessions.phase_label: Initial template implementation and interactive-field redesign
Final Word-template feedback and PowerPoint planning

requirements.title: Complete Style Set Across Word Templates
requirements.definition: All required active styles from the supplied design system must be present and consistently available across the applicable Word templates.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers completeness and cross-template availability of the style set; typography, list mechanics, captions, naming, and colors remain separate because they have independent acceptance criteria.

requirements.title: Template Typography and Style Spacing
requirements.definition: Heading, title, body, and related text styles must use the client-confirmed font sizes, emphasis, and readable spacing.
requirements.boundary_note: Font size, boldness, and style spacing are attributes of one typography mechanism; bullet geometry and caption formatting are independently testable and excluded.

requirements.title: Word Style Naming Convention
requirements.definition: Active Word styles must follow the agreed recognizable naming convention, including the proposed PBU prefix and localized naming where confirmed.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers style identifiers only; the document's default proofing language and visible field labels are separate behaviors.

requirements.title: Image and Table Caption Style
requirements.definition: Image and table caption text must have the agreed Century Gothic italic formatting and specified size treatment.
requirements.boundary_note: Caption formatting has its own named style and acceptance criterion, so it is separate from general typography.

requirements.title: Controlled Template Theme Colors
requirements.definition: Templates must include the intended theme colors while limiting users to the approved color palette rather than exposing inappropriate extra colors.
requirements.boundary_note: Color availability can change independently of typography and list behavior and therefore remains a separate Requirement.

requirements.title: Tab-Controlled List Hierarchy
requirements.definition: Relevant list styles must support intuitive Tab-based movement through consistently aligned nested list levels.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers level transitions and hierarchy mechanics; bullet appearance and double-digit numbering alignment can fail independently and are separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Graphic Bullet Appearance
requirements.definition: Graphic bullets must use the customer-approved design, remain proportionate to text, align vertically, and include the required level-specific variants.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers bullet geometry and visual treatment, not list-level navigation or numbered-list alignment.

requirements.title: Stable Numbered-List Alignment
requirements.definition: Numbered lists must retain correct alignment when numbering reaches two or more digits.
requirements.boundary_note: The double-digit alignment defect has a distinct failure condition from general Tab-based hierarchy and bullet appearance.

requirements.title: Danish Default Document Language
requirements.definition: The Word templates must use Danish as their default document language for the Danish organization.
requirements.boundary_note: Default document language is independent of style names and the visible Danish text used inside form fields.

requirements.title: Robust Editable Text Fields
requirements.definition: Ordinary fill-in areas must use a robust, readily editable field or placeholder approach rather than inappropriate password-dependent legacy controls.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the underlying choice of editable text-field mechanism; clear-on-click, help labels, specialized selectors, and multiline entry have independent behaviors.

requirements.title: Clear Placeholder Text on Activation
requirements.definition: Activating a fill-in field must allow the user to start typing without manually selecting and deleting its placeholder text.
requirements.boundary_note: Clear-on-activation is independently testable from whether a field has a label, preserves formatting, or supports multiple lines.

requirements.title: Localized Persistent Field Help Labels
requirements.definition: Interactive fields must have Danish labels matching their intended field text so users can recover the field's purpose after replacing its visible content.
requirements.boundary_note: Combines label language, semantic matching, and persistence as attributes of one field-help mechanism; it excludes the separate clear-on-click interaction.

requirements.title: Dropdown and Checklist Controls
requirements.definition: The appropriate Board Meeting and Board Recommendation fields must retain or receive functional dropdown and checklist controls.
requirements.boundary_note: Dropdowns and checklists are specialized selectors retained despite changes to ordinary text fields; date selection is a separate control.

requirements.title: Consistent Calendar Date Fields
requirements.definition: Applicable templates must provide the same calendar-style date selection behavior, using the client-approved day/month/year presentation.
requirements.boundary_note: Calendar selection and date formatting form one mechanism that can be modified independently of other dropdowns and text fields.

requirements.title: Multiline Entry in Interactive Fields
requirements.definition: Designated interactive text areas must support ordinary Enter-based multiline entry where users may need more than one line.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers whether fields accept multiple paragraphs; paragraph spacing after a hard return and automatic list numbering are separate behaviors.

requirements.title: Independent Non-Duplicating Field Content
requirements.definition: Interactive fields must be uniquely bound so editing one field does not duplicate or mirror content into another unintended location.
requirements.boundary_note: Content duplication is an independent data-binding failure and is not equivalent to placeholder clearing or table layout instability.

requirements.title: Preserve Formatting During Field Editing
requirements.definition: Editing designated interactive fields, including the title field, must preserve their assigned formatting.
requirements.boundary_note: Formatting retention can fail while a field remains editable, so it is separate from field architecture and clear-on-click behavior.

requirements.title: Legacy-to-New Template Copy-Paste Stability
requirements.definition: Content moved from legacy PBU documents into the new templates must retain predictable structure and formatting as robustly as Word permits.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers migration of existing content; table containment, list hierarchy, and line-break behavior are independently observable consequences with their own Requirements.

requirements.title: Natural Paragraph and Line-Break Behavior
requirements.definition: Users must be able to create ordinary line or paragraph breaks, including after pasted text, without excessive spacing or requiring knowledge of Shift+Enter.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers paragraph-style response to hard and soft returns; whether a content-control field permits multiple lines is handled separately.

requirements.title: Stable Table Layout Within Page Bounds
requirements.definition: Tables must remain usable, retain their structure, and stay within page margins during pasting and normal editing.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers table structure and page containment; text-box wrapping and Board Meeting row insertion have separate editing mechanisms.

requirements.title: Text-Box Word Wrap Without Column Displacement
requirements.definition: Text boxes must wrap growing text automatically rather than pushing adjacent columns outside the intended layout.
requirements.boundary_note: Word wrapping has a distinct trigger and outcome from table-paste stability and fixed-margin behavior.

requirements.title: Stable Content Margins and Spacing
requirements.definition: Template content regions must maintain fixed margins and appropriate internal spacing so text does not touch borders, clip graphics, or destabilize the page layout.
requirements.boundary_note: Margins and cell padding are attributes of one containment mechanism; line-break semantics and text-box wrapping remain separate.

requirements.title: Page Numbering Starts on Page Two
requirements.definition: The first page must omit its footer page number while numbering is displayed from page two onward.
requirements.boundary_note: Pagination visibility is independently configurable and unrelated to general margins or typography.

requirements.title: Consistent Rendering Across Users
requirements.definition: Templates must render and behave consistently for different users running current Microsoft Word on Windows.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers environment-level consistency rather than any single bullet, table, or form-field defect.

requirements.title: Board Meeting Field Alignment
requirements.definition: The Board Meeting template's Item and Title fields must align with Topic, Proposal, and Start Time.
requirements.boundary_note: Field alignment is independently verifiable from row insertion and border behavior in the same template.

requirements.title: Board Meeting Row Extension Workflow
requirements.definition: Users must be able to add another Board Meeting item through the agreed row-insertion and field-copy workflow without unintended borders or malformed numbering.
requirements.boundary_note: Treats row insertion, copied controls, numbering, and border continuity as tightly coupled parts of one structured-item extension workflow.

requirements.title: Complete Versioned Word Template Package
requirements.definition: Each delivery round must provide a complete package of the applicable Word templates using the client-specified common version designation.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a concrete delivery artifact and naming obligation, not a generic status or deployment Requirement.

requirements.title: Template Due-Diligence Assessment
requirements.definition: Perform an initial bounded assessment of the supplied templates and document identified errors, risks, task breakdown, and estimates.
requirements.boundary_note: The independently requested assessment report is the deliverable; routine later testing and debugging are evidence for product Requirements rather than part of this Requirement.

requirements.title: PowerPoint Template From Customer Design
requirements.definition: Create a new PowerPoint template from scratch using the customer's supplied design and graphic assets, with editable layouts suitable for real user content.
requirements.boundary_note: The PowerPoint work is represented as one provisional deliverable because most detailed layout points remain questions rather than independently confirmed requirements; later implementation evidence may justify splitting it.

unresolved_candidates.description: The client requires Danish as the default, while the freelancer states that the document will default to English with Danish style names. Event extraction should preserve the client requirement and treat any unresolved technical conflict separately.

Some bullet failures may result from using Tab rather than the style ribbon. Evidence does not yet fully resolve whether every reported case is an implementation defect, a user-workflow limitation, or both.

The exact final architecture for ordinary text areas is not fully explicit: plain editable text, modern content controls, and visible duplicated help text are discussed. The behavioral Requirements are separable, but the implementation choice may need audit.

The Master-template report that tables do not work and text is duplicated lacks the attached examples. Routing to table stability versus field-content uniqueness is plausible but should be verified from local evidence.

PowerPoint details such as logo placement, image masks, bullet capacity, backgrounds, and heading spacing are posed as design questions and are not yet sufficiently confirmed to become separate Requirement Atoms.
